14:T644,As multimodal resources are transformed into media outputs, agentic AI is expected to stay aligned with design intent over long horizons. Designers follow briefs specifying goals, constraints, and deliverables, with later work building on earlier decisions. Recent work reuses design experience across tasks, yet alignment among artifacts within one project remains challenging. Agents therefore need to preserve and apply this intent across domains and as projects grow. We introduce Design Anything, a graph-based harness that preserves design intent outside the model and binds deliverables to the workflow steps that produce them through an intent–execution graph. A task contract retains constraints and decisions, selected designs become explicit inputs to later generations, and a deterministic controller uses bindings and execution records to check output types and counts, identify outstanding deliverables, and guide subsequent turns. We also introduce DesignAnything-Bench, with 228 tasks across 19 design domains, including 38 project families at scales of 6, 14, and 24 artifacts. With the LLM held fixed, Design Anything satisfies 85.0% and 92.5% of the brief's factual constraints with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash High and GPT-5.6 Sol High, respectively, exceeding the strongest same-model baselines by 15.4% and 14.4%. These gains reach 25.1% and 23.0% on 24-artifact tasks. Under each model, Design Anything leads or ties in constraint satisfaction in 18 of 19 domains. Professional designers also prefer its complete deliverable sets over those of same-model baselines in a blind evaluation.8:["$","section",null,{"id":"abstract","className":"py-12","children":[["$","div",null,{"children":[["$","h2",null,{"className":"text-2xl font-semibold","children":"Abstract"}],null]}],["$","p",null,{"className":"mt-6 leading-relaxed","children":"$14"}]]}]

17:T1ddb,LUMA | AI glasses and a charging case for everyday transitions

We are developing LUMA for adults who want to capture a moment during an urban pause and move comfortably between work and leisure. The system comprises one complete pair of AI glasses and one matching charging/storage case. Connected assistance uses an intentionally captured image and a short, user-initiated spoken question through a paired phone. The glasses themselves are the main design task: two clear non-display lenses, a complete frame, folding temples, integrated electronics, comfortable contact surfaces and reachable physical controls. Print "LUMA" on the glasses and case.

The glasses mass target is at most 42 g. Choose a front width of 140–150 mm and a hinge-axis-to-tip centreline length of 135–150 mm for each temple; the largest temple section is at most 18 mm high and 12 mm thick. Folded glasses fit within 150 × 60 × 48 mm; the closed case fits within 170 × 85 × 65 mm, with at least 2 mm cavity clearance on each opposing side of the chosen folded envelope. Use the eleven recorded electronic modules, with 1 mm between envelopes and 1 mm enclosure outside them except at functional openings. The right-temple underside carries two flush pads of diameter 2 mm, spaced 6 mm centre to centre, both within 60 mm of the hinge; P+ is nearer the hinge. Matching case tips have diameter 1.2 mm. Use satin TR90 for the frame and temple shells, anodised aluminium hinges and silicone nose and ear contact surfaces. Develop the colour palette. Make B01 accessible for user replacement and print "User-replaceable B01" beside its removal detail.

The three glasses states are READY, CAPTURE and PRIVACY. READY exposes the camera with its indicator off; CAPTURE exposes the camera with a steady white front indicator; PRIVACY closes an opaque slider over the camera and disables camera and microphone capture. Give the slider a visible position mark. Folded glasses dock with the slider closed; the case indicator is steady amber during charging and off during stored/idle. Its indicator remains visible with the lid closed. Label these states on their corresponding design boards.

Audience: the product owner, industrial design team and engineering team, choosing the complete eyewear concept and preparing its first development brief.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the shared product, fit, operation, material and context facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. 03-module-records.md contains the eleven electronic module records. module-envelopes.en.md gives their local dimensions and permitted regions. charging-interface.en.md records pad geometry and mating relationships. module-and-docking-constraints.png diagrams the module envelopes and local charging interface. wearer-contact-map.png supplies the shared wearer and contact-zone reference across the directions. everyday-pause-reference.png supplies atmosphere for an urban pause and a warm office desk.

Deliverables:
1. Three distinct complete-product direction boards, each showing the glasses open and folded beside their matching case
2. One written selection sheet naming the chosen direction and the frame, temple and case decisions carried forward
3. Two specification sheets: a component and state sheet listing all eleven module IDs, envelope dimensions, connections, selected dimensions, pad-centre positions and operating-state changes; a material zoning and finish sheet listing materials, surface treatments, colour codes and contact zones
4. Six selected-glasses anatomy and detail boards: one front/top/right orthographic and component anatomy with schematic wiring and B01 replacement explosion; one front three-quarter view; one rear three-quarter view; one folded underside view; one nose-contact detail; and one ear-contact and hinge detail
5. Five operation and wearing boards: W1 everyday in READY with a nose/ear inset; CAPTURE with button reach and the white indicator; W2 work pause in PRIVACY with the closed slider and button inhibition; W3 commute pause in READY with a clear temple side view; and W4 cafe pause in PRIVACY with folded glasses held above the open case before contact
6. Four case boards: open charging with module placement, contact section and cavity dimensions; closed stored/idle with an empty open-case inset and outer dimensions; an enlarged empty-case interior; and a removal sequence with the fully folded glasses lifted by the frame/temple region
7. One material and colour application board for the selected glasses and case, mapping the material specification onto exterior, interior and skin-contact surfaces
8. One 12-second use-and-storage video moving through READY, CAPTURE, PRIVACY, folded docking with amber charging indication and closed-case stored/idle
9. One development presentation of at least 12 pages, reusing the directions, selection, both specifications, anatomy, details, operation, case and material work

Acceptance:
- On the three direction boards, present three named alternatives before the selection sheet; on that sheet and the presentation's first page, identify one selected direction, then develop its frame, temples and case in both specifications and every subsequent application.
- On the component specification, orthographic anatomy, folded underside and case boards, repeat the same selected open/folded dimensions and pad-centre positions. Dimension the 140–150 mm front-width range, 135–150 mm temple-length range, 18 × 12 mm section limit, 150 × 60 × 48 mm folded limit, 170 × 85 × 65 mm case limit and at least 2 mm cavity clearance on all six sides except marked support/contact interfaces; match openings, seams and hinge positions across all six anatomy/detail boards.
- On the component specification and orthographic anatomy, repeat all eight glasses module IDs, recorded envelopes and local-axis orientations; on that specification and the open charging board, repeat CB01, CC01 and U01 and their recorded envelopes. Show 1 mm envelope separation and enclosure, K01's 4 mm aperture, I01 within 12 mm of its centre, and B01's access cover, detachable connection and removal arrow labelled User-replaceable B01 on the anatomy board.
- On the component specification, operation boards, video and presentation, repeat READY, CAPTURE and PRIVACY with the prescribed camera, light and slider states. Label W1, W2, W3 and W4 on their assigned boards; show the W1 and W3 contact placements matching the nose/ear detail boards, button inhibition in W2, and folded glasses with the shutter closed and charging indication off before contact in W4.
- On the charging and folded underside boards, repeat the 2 mm pads, 6 mm spacing, 1.2 mm case tips and chosen pad-centre distances within 60 mm of the right hinge, with P+ nearer the hinge. Across the four case boards and video, preserve the keyed seat, parallel mating faces, lens-clear frame supports and removal access; show amber charging indication after docking and the visible indicator off in closed stored/idle.
- On the material specification, material application board and presentation, repeat satin TR90 shells, anodised aluminium hinges, silicone contacts and the selected colour codes; apply them consistently across the six anatomy/detail boards, five operation/wearing boards, four case boards and video. Show LUMA on the glasses and case, and reuse those labelled views with both specifications in the presentation's minimum 12 pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.18:T21e7,# LUMA — shared client facts

## Product

- Project name: LUMA.
- Product quantity: one complete adult-use AI glasses concept and one matching charging/storage case.
- Product intent: connected assistance interpreting an intentionally captured image and a short user-initiated spoken question through a paired phone.
- Capture initiation: deliberate user action.
- Physical scope: complete eyewear form, integrated components, contact surfaces, physical controls and charging/storage case.
- Lens configuration: two clear non-display lenses.
- Frame configuration: one bridge with two nose-contact regions, two folding temples and two ear-contact regions.
- Design choices: overall form, component arrangement within permitted regions, colours, hinge construction, folding order and case construction.
- Shared inputs: complete records for tiers 6, 14 and 24.
- Required product marking: LUMA on the glasses and case.
- Required replacement-detail wording: User-replaceable B01.

## Electronic module records

| module_id | name | quantity | local_x_mm | local_y_mm | local_z_mm | permitted_region |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C01 | Compute module | 1 | 28 | 8 | 5 | Either temple |
| B01 | Left battery envelope | 1 | 30 | 7 | 4 | Left temple |
| B02 | Right battery envelope | 1 | 30 | 7 | 4 | Right temple |
| S01 | Left speaker envelope | 1 | 16 | 5 | 3 | Left temple near ear |
| S02 | Right speaker envelope | 1 | 16 | 5 | 3 | Right temple near ear |
| K01 | Camera envelope | 1 | 8 | 8 | 6 | One outer front-frame corner |
| M01 | Microphone envelope | 1 | 4 | 3 | 2 | Frame or forward temple |
| I01 | Capture indicator envelope | 1 | 3 | 2 | 1 | Front beside K01 |
| CB01 | Case battery envelope | 1 | 45 | 25 | 6 | Case |
| CC01 | Case charging-board envelope | 1 | 20 | 15 | 4 | Case |
| U01 | Case input connector envelope | 1 | 12 | 5 | 7 | Case wall |

## Envelope integration

- Dimension basis: rectangular local X/Y/Z keep-out envelopes in mm.
- Module instances: exactly the quantities in the module table.
- Envelope orientation: rotation permitted; original dimensions retained; local axes identified in the anatomy.
- Envelope separation: at least 1 mm between separate envelopes.
- Enclosure allowance: at least 1 mm outside each solid envelope except at its functional opening.
- Glasses module set: C01, B01, B02, S01, S02, K01, M01, I01.
- Case module set: CB01, CC01, U01.
- Wiring representation: schematic routes between the recorded modules.
- Batteries: enclosed envelopes.
- Functional openings: camera, speakers and microphone; remaining module surfaces enclosed.
- U01 interface: USB-C-shaped input-connector envelope, socket mouth exposed at the case wall.
- Case charging context: unplugged operation from its internal battery.
- B01 service arrangement: user-accessible cover, detachable connection and illustrated removal direction.

## Physical dimensions

| Feature | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Open-glasses overall front width | Selected value from 140 to 150 mm |
| Each temple, hinge axis to tip along centreline | Selected value from 135 to 150 mm |
| Each temple, largest section height | At most 18 mm |
| Each temple, largest section thickness | At most 12 mm |
| Folded glasses envelope, width × depth × height | At most 150 × 60 × 48 mm |
| Closed case envelope, width × depth × height | At most 170 × 85 × 65 mm |
| Usable cavity clearance | At least 2 mm on each opposing side of all three axes of the selected folded envelope |
| Local clearance exceptions | Explicitly marked support and charging-contact interfaces |
| Glasses mass target | At most 42 g; unmeasured |

- Dimension records: actual selected open width, both temple lengths, largest temple sections, folded width/depth/height, cavity width/depth/height and closed-case width/depth/height.
- Contact surfaces: smooth rounded transitions and compliant nose/ear material.
- Skin-contact zoning: smooth surfaces separated from sharp edges, open ports and charging pads.
- Speaker openings: outward/downward near the ears; ear canals remain open.
- K01 position: forward-facing at one selected outer front-frame corner.
- K01 clear optical aperture: diameter 4 mm.
- I01 position: outward on the front; centre within 12 mm of the camera-aperture centre; visible with the shutter closed.
- M01 opening: outward, away from skin and the hinge.
- Capture button: reachable while worn, with the camera aperture clear and lenses free from finger pressure.
- Hinge relationship: each rigid module wholly on one side of a moving hinge.
- Folding relationship: separate, non-intersecting temple volumes in the folded state.

## Two-pad docking

| Element | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Glasses pad location | Underside of the right temple |
| Glasses pad quantity and labels | Exactly two; P+ and P− |
| Glasses pad geometry | Circular, flush, diameter 2 mm |
| Glasses pad spacing | 6 mm centre to centre along the temple |
| Pad-centre region | Both within the first 60 mm from the hinge axis towards the tip |
| Pad order | P+ nearer the hinge; P− nearer the tip |
| Pad-centre positions | Selected distances recorded in the design |
| Case contact tips | Two; diameter 1.2 mm; 6 mm centre spacing |
| Polarity alignment | P+ to P+ and P− to P− |
| Contact faces | Parallel at docking |
| Docking orientation | Visible locating/keying feature identifying the matching orientation |
| Docking state | Fully folded glasses; privacy slider closed |
| Charging state | Glasses seated; both pads mated; separate case indicator steadily amber |
| Stored/idle state | Same glasses seated; case indicator off; case closed |
| Case indicator location | Visible with the lid closed |
| Case support | Frame/temple regions; lenses clear of direct supporting pressure |
| Closed-lid relationship | All components contained within the closed case |
| Removal access | Finger access to frame/temple regions |
| Empty-case state | Open cavity with the same supports, contacts and locating feature |
| Prototype topics | Spring travel, force and circuit protection |

## Operating states

| State | Camera aperture | Front capture indicator | Control and capture behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| READY | Uncovered | Off | Ready for deliberate user initiation; no active capture |
| CAPTURE | Uncovered | Steadily white during the illustrated active interval | Visible user-operated capture button; active capture |
| PRIVACY | Entire aperture covered by an opaque physical slider | Off | Visible physical position mark; camera and microphone capture disabled; pressing capture does not start capture |

## Wearing and handling contexts

| Code | Name | Context | Glasses state | View and handling facts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | everyday | Adult standing during a quiet urban pause | READY | Fully open glasses on the face; three-quarter upper-body view; close inset of nose/ear placement |
| W2 | work pause | Adult seated at a desk | PRIVACY | Glasses worn; closed shutter visible; hand near the reachable capture button; capture inhibited |
| W3 | commute pause | Adult standing in a stationary sheltered transit waiting area | READY | Clear side view of the same temple and ear contact |
| W4 | cafe pause | Adult at a cafe table | PRIVACY | Same fully folded glasses held by the frame/temple region before placement in the same open case; shutter closed; charging indication off before contact; consistent relative scale |

- Board labels: W codes and corresponding READY or PRIVACY state labels.
- People, clothing and surroundings: open design choices within the recorded contexts.
- Product continuity: selected dimensions and component identities shared across every context.
- Face geometry: open; contact-zone illustration supplies relative locations.
- Contact/operation insets: part of their parent boards.

## Materials and development records

- Frame and temple shells: TR90; satin finish.
- Hinges: anodised aluminium.
- Nose and ear contact surfaces: silicone; smooth rounded transitions.
- Case materials and finishes: selected in the design.
- Colour palette: selected in the design; colour codes recorded with material applications.
- Prototype topics: mass, fit/comfort, hinge life, thermal behaviour, charging reliability and capture/privacy interlock.
- Unspecified performance fields: component mass, battery capacity, runtime, charging time, optical prescription, waterproof rating and drop rating.
- U01 unspecified electrical fields: standard, power rating and charging protocol.
- Source ownership: original repository-authored text, local component drawings and records; redistributable with the commission.

1b:T5199,# LUMA — Direction Selection Sheet

**Document type:** presentation document; **stage:** process; **format:** A4. **No images.** This written record closes the direction phase and releases the selected concept into development.

---

## Page 1 — Direction selection

### 1. Purpose

This sheet records the closure of the LUMA direction phase and releases the selected concept into development. It states the selected direction, the alternatives shown, the reasons for selection, and the locked schedule that all later work must repeat.

### 2. Alternatives shown

The three alternatives were presented in the following order.

#### 2.1 (A) Continuum — seamless minimal

Continuum is a monobloc brow line with no visible parting seam, a flush buried anodised aluminium hinge cover, satin graphite TR90 with a bone-white inner rim, one slim machined shutter track with a visible position mark, and a soft rounded pebble case in the matching graphite tone.

#### 2.2 (B) Softline — rounded organic

Softline uses generous radii, a warm sand TR90 shell with a clay inner rim and a soft-touch temple, a sculpted shutter ridge, and a case with a wrapped textile-look lid.

#### 2.3 (C) Precision — engineered

Precision uses an exposed anodised aluminium hinge barrel, crisp graphic seam lines, ink blue and graphite TR90 with silver metal, a recessed pocket around the charging pads, and a case with an exposed machined contact block.

### 3. Decision

Selected direction: Continuum — seamless minimal.

### 4. Status of other directions

Softline and Precision are retained for reference only and are not developed further.

---

## Page 2 — Why Continuum

### 1. Reasoning for selection

Continuum is selected because its unbroken brow and buried hinge cover produce one continuous surface with no seam and no exposed barrel. This suits a product handled in an office and on the street: it reads as a complete object rather than an assembly of parts, and it gives fewer places for clothing, hair or desk surfaces to catch on visible mechanisms. The graphite and bone satin TR90 palette is quiet enough to pass as ordinary eyewear while the LUMA family is still recognisable. The bone inner rim gives a single controlled accent exactly where the wearer sees it when the glasses are folded. The rounded pebble case extends the same surface language to the dock, so the closed case reads as part of the same object rather than as a separate accessory. These choices support the fixed product intent: a complete adult-use AI glasses concept with a matching charging/storage case, deliberate capture initiation, and everyday wearing contexts.

### 2. Softline

Softline was not carried forward because its warm tactile palette and wrapped textile lid move away from the neutral product language established for LUMA. The wrapped lid also adds a surface that collects dirt in the handled case routine. Its rounded organic language is coherent, but it would make the product family less directly comparable to the selected graphite and bone material direction.

### 3. Precision

Precision was not carried forward because, although coherent, its exposed hinge barrel, graphic seams and recessed pad pocket read as more mechanical than an everyday brief asks for. The exposed barrel and graphic seams would draw attention to assembly details that Continuum resolves into a continuous surface. Its machined contact block and recessed pad pocket are technically legible, but they are less consistent with the quiet wearable form selected for LUMA.

### 4. Continuity with product requirements

Continuum remains within the fixed requirements: two clear non-display lenses, a frame with one bridge and two nose-contact regions, two folding temples and two ear-contact regions, a camera at one outer front-frame corner, an opaque physical privacy shutter, a flush capture control, user-replaceable B01 in the left temple, and a case with internal charging contacts and a closed-lid indicator. It also preserves the required product marking LUMA on the glasses and case and the required replacement-detail wording User-replaceable B01.

---

## Page 3 — Frame decisions carried forward

### 1. Statement of intent

The frame will carry the Continuum form language: a calm, continuous front that looks like ordinary eyewear, with the camera, indicator, microphone and shutter integrated without turning the front into a technical display.

### 2. Frame decisions

| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Lens configuration | Two clear non-display lenses. |
| Frame configuration | One bridge with two nose-contact regions, two folding temples and two ear-contact regions. |
| Brow | Monobloc brow line with no visible parting seam. |
| Inner rim | Bone-white inner rim, matching LUMA-C02 Bone in satin TR90. |
| Hinge cover | Flush buried anodised aluminium hinge cover. |
| Front width | Open front width, hinge axis to hinge axis: 146 mm (permitted range 140 to 150 mm). |
| Camera | K01 at the outer front corner of the right frame, forward-facing; clear optical aperture diameter 4 mm. |
| Capture indicator | I01 beside K01 on the front, outward; centre 9.0 mm from the camera-aperture centre, within 12 mm, visible when the shutter is closed. |
| Shutter | Opaque slider over the camera; travel 9 mm; visible position mark; closed position is PRIVACY. |
| Microphone | M01 in the frame or forward temple, opening outward, away from skin and the hinge. |
| Materials | Frame and temple shells in TR90, satin finish; hinges in anodised aluminium. |
| Skin contact | Nose-contact surfaces in silicone LUMA-C04 Smoke, smooth rounded transitions, separated from sharp edges, open ports and charging pads. |

### 3. State relationship

The frame must support the three operating states. In READY, the camera aperture is uncovered and the front capture indicator is off; no active capture is present. In CAPTURE, the aperture is uncovered, the front capture indicator is steadily white during the illustrated active interval, and the visible user-operated capture button is used for active capture. In PRIVACY, the entire aperture is covered by the opaque physical slider, the indicator is off, a visible physical position mark is present, camera and microphone capture are disabled, and pressing capture does not start capture.

### 4. Marking

The required product marking LUMA appears on the glasses. The required replacement-detail wording User-replaceable B01 is carried with the left-temple battery service arrangement.

## Page 4 — Temple decisions carried forward

### 1. Statement of intent

The temples will be slim, straight and tapered, so the glasses remain ordinary in silhouette while the modules, hinge and charging interface are contained cleanly.

### 2. Temple decisions

| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Form | Slim straight temples tapering to the tip. |
| Largest temple section | 16 mm high by 10 mm thick (limits: not more than 18 mm high, not more than 12 mm thick). |
| Temple length | 142 mm, both temples equal, hinge axis to tip along the centreline (permitted range 135 to 150 mm). |
| Hinge construction | Anodised aluminium; each rigid module wholly on one side of a moving hinge. |

| Charging pads | Two flush circular pads on the underside of the right temple, diameter 2 mm, centres 6 mm apart. P+ centre 18 mm and P- centre 24 mm behind the hinge axis, both within 60 mm of the hinge, P+ nearer the hinge. |
| Battery service | B01 left battery envelope in the left temple; user-accessible cover, detachable connection and illustrated removal direction; required wording User-replaceable B01. |

All module quantities are exactly as recorded. Envelope separation is at least 1 mm between separate envelopes, and enclosure allowance is at least 1 mm outside each solid envelope except at its functional opening. Speaker openings are outward/downward near the ears, and the ear canals remain open. Ear-contact surfaces use silicone LUMA-C04 Smoke with smooth rounded transitions.

### 4. Service and handling

The temple form keeps skin-contact zoning separate from sharp edges, open ports and charging pads. The two-pad docking is local to the underside of the right temple and does not alter the complete temple or case forms. Docking occurs with the glasses fully folded and the privacy slider closed. The selected pad positions remain within the first 60 mm from the hinge axis towards the tip.

## Page 5 — Case decisions carried forward

### 1. Statement of intent

The case will be a rounded pebble dock in the same Continuum surface language, holding the folded glasses securely, exposing the charging interface only where needed, and reading as part of the same product family.

### 2. Case decisions

| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Form | Rounded pebble form. |
| Shell | Graphite shell. |
| Marking | Bone-white LUMA print on the lid. |

| Closed envelope | 168 by 78 by 62 mm. |

| Module set | CB01, CC01, U01. |
| Materials | Case materials and finishes selected in the design; LUMA-C05 Warm Grey flocked case tray. |

### 3. Docking and charging

The docking orientation uses a visible locating/keying feature identifying the matching orientation. In the docking state the glasses are fully folded and the privacy slider is closed. In the charging state the glasses are seated, both pads are mated, and the separate case indicator is steadily amber. In the stored/idle state the same glasses are seated, the case indicator is off, and the case is closed. The case support uses frame/temple regions; lenses remain clear of direct supporting pressure. The closed-lid relationship contains all components within the closed case. Removal access provides finger access to frame/temple regions. The empty-case state presents an open cavity with the same supports, contacts and locating feature.

### 4. Case modules and power

CB01 is the case battery envelope, CC01 is the case charging-board envelope, and U01 is the case input connector envelope. U01 is a USB-C-shaped input-connector envelope with its socket mouth exposed at the case wall. The case charging context is unplugged operation from its internal battery. The internal cavity clearance per side of the folded envelope is 3.5 mm width, 6 mm depth, 4 mm height; the minimum is 2 mm on every opposing side, and the formed docking seat and the two 1.2 mm charge-contact tips are the explicit local exceptions marked as support and charging-contact interfaces.

## Page 7 — What the decision fixes and what stays open

### 1. Fixed by the selection

The direction is fixed as Continuum — seamless minimal. Softline and Precision are retained for reference only and are not developed further. The locked schedule is fixed and must be repeated without change. The glasses use two clear non-display lenses, a monobloc brow with no visible parting seam, a bone-white inner rim, a flush buried anodised aluminium hinge cover, a right-front camera with a 4 mm clear optical aperture, a capture indicator 9.0 mm from the camera-aperture centre, an opaque 9 mm shutter slider with a visible position mark and PRIVACY closed position, and a flush right-temple capture button 42 mm behind the hinge axis. The temples use the selected 142 mm length and 16 mm by 10 mm largest section. The right temple carries the two flush charging pads with P+ at 18 mm and P- at 24 mm behind the hinge axis. The case uses the rounded pebble form, graphite shell, bone-white LUMA lid print, keyed seat, 1.2 mm contact tips at 6 mm spacing, internal cavity 154 by 64 by 48 mm, and closed envelope 168 by 78 by 62 mm. The palette is fixed as LUMA-C01 through LUMA-C05.

### 2. Fixed by the component records

The module set for the glasses is C01, B01, B02, S01, S02, K01, M01 and I01. The case module set is CB01, CC01 and U01. Quantities are exactly as recorded. Envelope orientation may rotate; original dimensions are retained; local axes are identified in the anatomy. Each module remains within its permitted region. Envelope separation is at least 1 mm between separate envelopes, and enclosure allowance is at least 1 mm outside each solid envelope except at its functional opening. Functional openings are limited to camera, speakers and microphone; remaining module surfaces are enclosed. Batteries are enclosed envelopes. B01 uses a user-accessible cover, detachable connection and illustrated removal direction, with the required replacement-detail wording User-replaceable B01. U01 keeps its USB-C-shaped socket mouth exposed at the case wall.

### 3. Open for prototyping

Spring travel, force and electrical protection remain to be prototyped. The glasses mass is a target, not yet measured. The following performance fields remain unspecified: component mass, battery capacity, runtime, charging time, optical prescription, waterproof rating and drop rating. U01 electrical fields remain unspecified: standard, power rating and charging protocol. Prototype topics include mass, fit/comfort, hinge life, thermal behaviour, charging reliability and capture/privacy interlock. Case materials and finishes are selected in the design, but any remaining finish approvals and production tolerances remain open until prototype review.

### 4. State and context decisions that are fixed

The operating states are fixed. READY has an uncovered aperture, indicator off, and no active capture. CAPTURE has an uncovered aperture, a steadily white front capture indicator during the illustrated active interval, and active capture through the visible user-operated capture button. PRIVACY has the entire aperture covered by the opaque physical slider, indicator off, visible physical position mark, camera and microphone capture disabled, and capture inhibited. The wearing contexts are fixed for later boards: W1 everyday READY, W2 work pause PRIVACY, W3 commute pause READY, and W4 cafe pause PRIVACY. Product continuity across contexts is fixed: selected dimensions and component identities are shared across every context.

All later work must use the module IDs and quantities exactly as recorded: C01, B01, B02, S01, S02, K01, M01 and I01 for the glasses; CB01, CC01 and U01 for the case. People, clothing and surroundings remain open design choices within the recorded contexts; face geometry is open, and the contact-zone illustration supplies relative locations. Contact and operation insets are part of their parent boards.

### 4. Prototype and review consequence

The next stage must carry forward the prototype topics: spring travel, force and electrical protection; mass, fit/comfort, hinge life, thermal behaviour, charging reliability and capture/privacy interlock. The mass target remains 38 g with the limit not more than 42 g and the value unmeasured. Unspecified performance fields remain open until prototype results are recorded. The two-pad docking interface remains local to the underside of the right temple and must be shown with matching polarity, parallel contact faces and the visible locating/keying feature.

## Page 2

### 3. Envelope integration rules

The selected Continuum design applies the following integration rules to every recorded module envelope. There is at least 1 mm between separate envelopes. There is at least 1 mm outside every envelope except at its functional opening. Batteries are enclosed envelopes. The case and glasses shells, trays, liners, and supports are arranged so that no solid envelope is exposed except where a functional opening or an explicitly marked support or charging-contact interface requires local access.

In the glasses, the minimum required separation is achieved at the C01-to-B02 envelope pair in the right temple, where the recorded envelopes are separated by 1.5 mm along the temple centreline after the selected placement. The C01-to-B02 gap is the tightest module-to-module separation in the glasses. The left temple keeps B01 and S01 separated by more than 1 mm, and the right temple keeps B02 and S02 separated by more than 1 mm. The front-frame pair K01 and I01 is separated by more than 1 mm while I01 remains centred 9.0 mm from the camera-aperture centre. M01 is placed on the left front-frame outer lower edge and is separated from K01, I01, and the hinge region by more than 1 mm. In the case, the minimum required separation is achieved at the CB01-to-CC01 envelope pair, where the selected placement provides 2.0 mm clearance. CC01 and U01 are separated by at least 2.0 mm, and U01’s socket mouth is the only exposed surface of that envelope.

The 1 mm enclosure allowance is consumed by the shell in the sense that the innermost shell surface is offset at least 1 mm from each solid envelope, and the shell material and its compliant liners occupy the region outside that offset. In the right temple, the allowance around C01 and B02 is bounded by the inner TR90 shell and a thin compliant liner. In the left temple, the allowance around B01 and S01 is bounded by the inner TR90 shell. At the front frame, the allowance around K01 and I01 is bounded by the front shell except at the camera aperture and the indicator window. In the case, the allowance around CB01 and CC01 is bounded by the case shell and the flocked tray. At U01, the allowance terminates at the USB-C-shaped socket mouth. At the charging pads and case contact tips, the allowance is locally replaced by the explicitly marked support and charging-contact interfaces.

### 5. Schematic connection schedule

|---:|---|---|---|---|

| 19 | C01 Compute module | Paired phone | Data link | Image and question exchange through the paired phone link. |

**5.1 Capture chain.** The capture chain is explicit. The capture button is the deliberate user-operated input and connects to C01. C01 enables K01 and commands the capture interval, and K01 returns image data to C01. C01 drives I01 steadily white during the illustrated active interval. C01 exchanges the captured image and the short user-initiated spoken question with the paired phone through the link. M01 feeds the spoken question to C01. The microphone M01 is therefore part of the capture chain for the user-initiated spoken question, and it is disabled in PRIVACY.

## Page 6

### 7. Charging and docking interface

The local charging interface is on the underside of the right temple. It uses exactly two flush circular pads, labelled P+ and P−. Each pad has a diameter of 2 mm. The pad centres are 6 mm apart along the temple. P+ is nearer the hinge, with its centre 18 mm behind the hinge axis. P− is nearer the tip, with its centre 24 mm behind the hinge axis. Both pad centres are within the first 60 mm from the hinge axis towards the tip. The pads are flush with the local temple surface.

The case provides two contact tips. Each tip has a diameter of 1.2 mm. The tip centres are 6 mm apart. Polarity is aligned so that P+ mates with P+ and P− mates with P−. The contact faces are parallel at docking. A visible locating and keying feature identifies the matching orientation. The case has a keyed seat that receives the folded glasses. The formed docking seat and the two 1.2 mm contact tips are the explicit marked local exceptions to the general enclosure and clearance rules. The case supports the frame and temple regions; the lenses are clear of direct supporting pressure. In the closed-lid relationship, all components are contained within the closed case. Removal access is provided by finger access to the frame and temple regions. The empty-case state presents an open cavity with the same supports, contacts, and locating feature.

The docking state uses fully folded glasses with the privacy slider closed. In the charging state, the glasses are seated, both pads are mated, and the separate case indicator is steadily amber. In the stored or idle state, the same glasses are seated, the case indicator is off, and the case is closed. The case indicator is visible with the lid closed. Spring travel, force, and electrical protection remain to be prototyped. The U01 electrical fields of standard, power rating, and charging protocol also remain unspecified and must be resolved before production.

## Page 7

### 8. Operating states and appurtenant changes

The three operating states are READY, CAPTURE, and PRIVACY. The table below states the camera aperture, front capture indicator, control and capture behaviour, shutter position, camera availability, and microphone availability for each state.

**Table 8-1 — Operating states**

| State | Camera aperture | Front capture indicator | Control and capture behaviour | Shutter position | Camera availability | Microphone availability |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| READY | Uncovered | Off | Ready for deliberate user initiation; no active capture | Open, not covering the aperture | Available for capture when the user operates the capture button | Available for the user-initiated spoken question |
| CAPTURE | Uncovered | Steadily white during the illustrated active interval | Visible user-operated capture button; active capture | Open, not covering the aperture | Available; active capture | Available for the user-initiated spoken question |
| PRIVACY | Entire aperture covered by an opaque physical slider | Off | Visible physical position mark; camera and microphone capture disabled; pressing capture does not start capture | Closed over the aperture | Unavailable | Unavailable |

The changes between states are precise. From READY to CAPTURE, the shutter remains open and the camera aperture remains uncovered; the front capture indicator changes from off to steadily white during the illustrated active interval; the camera becomes active for capture; the microphone remains available for the user-initiated spoken question; and the capture button initiates the active capture. From READY or CAPTURE to PRIVACY, the opaque slider moves 9 mm to the closed position over the camera; the front capture indicator remains off; the camera is unavailable; microphone capture is disabled; and pressing capture does not start capture. From PRIVACY to READY, the slider opens, the camera aperture becomes uncovered, the indicator remains off, and the camera and microphone become available again only for deliberate user initiation.

The case behaviour is separate from the glasses state table. While charging, the case indicator is steadily amber. While stored or idle, the case indicator is off and the case is closed. The case indicator is visible with the lid closed. In the docked state, the folded glasses dock with the shutter closed. The bridge carries no docked indication until the tips make contact. Once the tips make contact and both pads are mated, the charging state can be indicated by the case indicator.

## Page 8

### 9. B01 service arrangement

B01 is the left battery envelope. It is located in the left temple, mid segment, 40 mm to 70 mm behind the hinge axis. The selected Continuum design provides a user-accessible cover on the left temple. The cover is flush with the satin TR90 shell in the closed position and is opened by the user without disturbing the optical front, the nose contact, or the ear contact. The battery envelope is an enclosed envelope during normal wear. The service arrangement exposes only the battery compartment when the cover is open.

The battery connection is detachable. The battery is not soldered in place. The removal direction is illustrated. The illustrated removal direction shows the cover opening direction and the direction in which the battery envelope is withdrawn from its detachable connection. The marking text “User-replaceable B01” is placed beside the removal detail. The marking is visible when the cover is open and the removal detail is exposed. The service arrangement retains the required enclosure of B01 when the cover is closed.

### 10. Open items

The following items remain to be prototyped and verified. They are not closed by this specification sheet.

**10.1 Mass and comfort.** The mass target is 38 g, with a limit of not more than 42 g; the mass is unmeasured. Component masses, total glasses mass, total case mass, fit, comfort, nose-contact pressure, and ear-contact pressure remain to be prototyped and verified.

**10.2 Hinge and folding.** Hinge life, folding order, folded-envelope repeatability, and the separation of the folded temple volumes remain to be verified. The selected dimensions are locked, but the hinge construction and folding order remain design choices within the Continuum direction.

**10.3 Thermal and electrical.** Thermal behaviour, battery capacity, runtime, charging time, charging reliability, and electrical protection remain to be prototyped and verified. The U01 electrical fields of standard, power rating, and charging protocol remain unspecified. The charging interface spring travel and force remain to be prototyped.

**10.4 Capture and privacy interlock.** The capture/privacy interlock remains to be prototyped and verified. Verification must confirm that pressing capture in PRIVACY does not start capture, that camera and microphone capture are disabled in PRIVACY, that the shutter travel is 9 mm, that the visible position mark is legible, and that I01 is visible when the shutter is closed.

**10.5 Docking and case behaviour.** Verification must confirm the keyed seat, the P+ to P+ and P− to P− polarity alignment, the parallel contact faces, the 6 mm centre spacing of the pads and tips, the 18 mm and 24 mm pad-centre positions behind the hinge axis, and the 60 mm limit from the hinge axis. The case indicator must be verified as steadily amber while charging and off while stored or idle, and it must remain visible with the lid closed.

**10.6 Envelope integration and tolerances.** Verification must confirm that every separate envelope maintains at least 1 mm separation after tolerance stack-up, that every solid envelope maintains at least 1 mm enclosure allowance except at its functional opening, and that the marked support and charging-contact interfaces are the only local exceptions. The case cavity clearance must be verified as 3.5 mm width, 6 mm depth, and 4 mm height per side, with a minimum of 2 mm on every opposing side, except at the formed docking seat and the two 1.2 mm contact tips.

**10.7 Unspecified performance fields.** The following remain unspecified and must be resolved before production: optical prescription, waterproof rating, drop rating, battery capacity, runtime, charging time, component mass, and the U01 electrical standard, power rating, and charging protocol.

**10.8 Material and colour application.** The colour palette is locked as LUMA-C01 Graphite (satin TR90), LUMA-C02 Bone (satin TR90), LUMA-C03 Silver (anodised aluminium), LUMA-C04 Smoke (silicone nose and ear contacts), and LUMA-C05 Warm Grey (flocked case tray). Colour codes, material applications, surface finishes, and the exact zoning of the satin TR90, anodised aluminium, silicone, and flocked tray must be recorded in the material and colour application deliverable.

## Page 1

## Section 1 — Scope and zoning principle

### 1.1 Purpose of this sheet

This sheet fixes the material zoning and finish specification for the selected Continuum direction of LUMA. It covers the complete glasses and the matching charging/storage case. It zones every surface into one of three families: exterior surfaces, interior and non-contact surfaces, and skin-contact surfaces. Each surface carries one material, one surface treatment and one colour code. The zoning is written for process stage, so it must be stable enough to guide later detailed design, tooling discussion and finish sampling.

### 1.2 Zoning families

Exterior surfaces are the surfaces visible when the product is worn, carried, docked or stored. They include the outer front, outer temples, outer case, shutter slider, capture button, camera bezel, case meeting gap and socket surround. These surfaces carry the Continuum body colour and the satin family finish unless a functional opening interrupts them.

Interior and non-contact surfaces are inside faces, service faces or functional lands that are not in sustained skin contact. They include the frame front interior, the inner front rim, lens edges, temple interiors, indicator windows, case tray, case seat and related internal surrounds. These surfaces may use the controlled Bone accent or the Warm Grey tray lining, but they do not introduce a second exterior body colour.

Skin-contact surfaces are exactly four regions: left nose contact, right nose contact, left ear contact and right ear contact. These four regions use compliant silicone only. They are Smoke, soft matte, and have smooth rounded transitions into and out of each contact area.

### 1.3 One material, one treatment, one colour code

Each surface in this sheet is assigned one material, one surface treatment and one colour code. The client-fixed materials are satin TR90 for the frame and temple shells, anodised aluminium for the hinge set, and silicone for the nose and ear contact surfaces. The colour choices are the developed Continuum palette recorded in Section 4 and repeated in locked form in Section 9. Functional optical, diffusing and contact surfaces are listed as functional surfaces; they do not add decorative colours to the palette.

### Table 1 — Zoning families and rules

| Family | Surfaces | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Exterior surfaces | Frame front exterior; left and right temple shell exteriors; temple tips; shutter slider; capture button; camera bezel; case exterior lid; case exterior body; case meeting gap; case input socket surround | One satin level across TR90. Graphite body colour. No gloss. No decorative metal except anodised aluminium. |
| Interior and non-contact surfaces | Frame front interior; inner front rim; left and right temple shell interiors; lens edges; indicator windows; case interior tray; case seat; case indicator window | Controlled accents allowed: Bone inner rim, Warm Grey tray. Matte or satin as specified. No skin-contact silicone. |
| Skin-contact surfaces | Left nose contact; right nose contact; left ear contact; right ear contact | Compliant silicone only. Smoke. Soft matte. Smooth rounded transitions. No sharp edges, ports or charging pads. |

## Page 3

## Section 3 — Surface treatments

### 3.1 Treatment intent

Surface treatments are specified so that a viewer sees one coherent object and a moulding engineer can inspect the tool and process. The TR90 satin finish is low sheen, with no visible moulding gloss and a fine uniform texture. It is the same on the frame and the temples. The anodised hinges are fine matte metallic, with no polished highlights. The silicone contact surfaces are soft matte, with smooth rounded transitions and no sharp edges. The case shell matches the frame’s satin. The case tray is a flocked matte. The shutter slider is satin so it reads as part of the front. The button is satin with a crisp edge.

### Table 3 — Surface treatment intent

| Element | Treatment intent | Inspection check |
|---|---|---|
| TR90 satin finish | Low sheen; no visible moulding gloss; fine uniform texture; same on frame and temples | Check gloss level at 60°; no flow marks; texture uniform across front and temples. |
| Anodised hinges | Fine matte metallic; no polished highlights | Check no bright buffed edges; uniform matte etch; colour within Silver. |
| Silicone contact surfaces | Soft matte; smooth rounded transitions; no sharp edges | Check radius at every transition; no flash; no glossy patches. |
| Case shell | Matches the frame’s satin | Check case lid and body against frame under same light; no gloss mismatch. |
| Case tray | Flocked matte | Check uniform fibre lay; no shiny areas; no loose flock. |
| Shutter slider | Satin, reads as part of front | Check slider closed: tone and sheen match front; no proud gloss strip. |
| Capture button | Satin with crisp edge | Check crisp perimeter; satin face; no polished bevel. |

### 3.2 Viewer and engineer checks

The viewer check is coherence. The frame, temples, case shell, shutter and button must read as one satin family. The engineer check is reproducibility. There is one texture, one gloss target and one masking rule. The hinges must read as metal but not as jewellery. The silicone must read as soft and quiet. The tray must read as a lining, not as an exterior surface. The shutter must disappear into the front when closed. The button must be findable by touch without becoming a glossy accent.

## Section 4 — Colour palette

### 4.1 Locked palette with developed hex mapping

Table 4 records the locked Continuum palette. The codes and names are locked. The hex values are the developed production mapping used by this sheet for sampling and specification.

### Table 4 — Locked palette

|---|---|---|---|

### 4.2 Palette logic, part one

Graphite is the body colour for both glasses and case so the family reads as one object. It carries the exterior shell, temples, case exterior, shutter, button and bezel. Bone is a single controlled interior accent used on the inner front rim and the markings. It is not used as a second exterior colour. Silver is reserved for metal only, so the aluminium reads as metal and nothing else pretends to be metal.

### 4.3 Palette logic, part two

Smoke is the contact material, kept visually quiet because it is the only part in constant skin contact. Warm Grey is used for the tray so the interior reads as a lining rather than a surface. Functional optical, diffusing and contact interfaces are not decorative colours. They are listed in Section 6 without adding to the palette. No later stage may make Bone an exterior body colour, make Silver a decorative trim, or make Smoke a general-purpose dark accent.

| User-replaceable B01 | Inside the left temple shell, immediately beside the B01 user-accessible cover, aligned with the illustrated removal direction | Durable matte pad print; beside the removal-direction illustration | LUMA-C02 Bone on LUMA-C01 Graphite |

### 7.2 Placement rules

The B01 marking is not placed on silicone, not on the charging pads and not across a hinge. The B01 cover is user-accessible, has a detachable connection and an illustrated removal direction; the wording sits on the flat land beside that detail. The case marking is outside the meeting gap and does not interfere with the locating/keying feature. All markings remain visible with the relevant cover or lid in its normal service position. The marking ink is matte and flush, so it does not create a gloss patch against the satin TR90.

## Page 9

## Section 8 — Finish consistency rules

### 8.1 Consistency rules

The following rules keep the family coherent. They apply to process and final stages. No later stage may introduce an additional finish or colour.

1. One satin level across every TR90 part. Frame front, both temple shells, case shell, shutter slider, capture button, camera bezel, case meeting gap and socket surround use the same satin TR90 finish.

2. Metal only where it is aluminium. Decorative metal is anodised aluminium in LUMA-C03 Silver on the hinge set and case contact block. Functional contact interfaces are not decorative and do not introduce a second metal colour.

3. Silicone only at the four contact regions. Nose and ear contact surfaces use LUMA-C04 Smoke silicone. No other surface uses skin-contact silicone.

4. Bone used only for the interior accent and markings. Inner front rim and all markings and prints use LUMA-C02 Bone. Bone is not an exterior body colour.

5. No additional finish or colour introduced at any later stage. No gloss, chrome, soft-touch coating, secondary paint, sticker or lens tint is added to the Continuum direction.

6. The case shell matches the frame’s satin. The case must not read as gloss, rubberised or fabric.

7. The case tray and seat are flocked matte in Warm Grey. They must not be changed to moulded gloss or hard plastic.

8. The shutter slider remains satin so it reads as part of the front. It must not become a glossy black window or a metallic strip.

9. The capture button remains satin with a crisp edge. It must not acquire a polished bevel or a different satin level.

10. All transitions into and out of skin-contact zones are smooth rounded transitions. No sharp edge, open port or charging pad lies inside a skin-contact zone.

11. Functional optical, diffusing and contact surfaces are listed as functional. They are not palette colours and must not be used to introduce a new accent.

28:T16f0,# TIDELINE LIBRARY — real site, historical baseline and client scenario

The supplied inputs are site-overhead.png (a real, locked 2019 orthorectified aerial with a marked design extent) and site-plan.png (a deterministic plan of the same extent and selected existing context), plus this text. Both boards use boundary A–D, grid north and metric scale. No existing library or proposed scheme is shown. The tested system receives the two PNG boards and this text.

## Actual site and source limits

The setting is a grass strip on the landward side of the Ohio River flood barrier at Cairo, Illinois, USA. The approximately 4,563 m² quadrilateral is an author-defined design extent inside the visible grass, not a cadastral parcel or assertion of ownership. It is approximately 145 m long and 24–39 m wide, with A–B / B–C / C–D / D–A sides of approximately 24 / 147 / 39 / 145 m. The 6,800 m² in the brief is proposed total gross floor area across floors and phases, not site area.

From west to east the existing relationship is: neighbourhood and city street; grass design extent; flood barrier; elevated railway corridor; riverbank; Ohio River. The railway is not a public promenade. Preserve the external flood barrier, railway, streets and adjoining properties. The commissioned levee-side public walk is a proposed landward interface within the design extent; orient the main entrance to it and connect it to the city sidewalk. No existing pedestrian crossing of the barrier or tracks is assumed. The public walk is a design requirement, not a feature claimed to exist in the aerial.

Plan alignments and the author boundary were digitised from the 2019 aerial with an estimated tracing uncertainty of about 2 m, not survey-certified accuracy. Two selected neighbouring roof outlines are shown; blank areas do not imply vacant land. See the real aerial for complete visible context. Gray road bands and line weights indicate corridors, not measured widths. Heights of neighbouring buildings, floodwall crest height and exact track/road widths are not established. The blank triangle over the far river is NoData outside the selected 2019 image footprint, not dry land. It has not been filled with AI or a different year's image.

## One explicit vertical datum

The real terrain source is a 1 m USGS 3DEP bare-earth DEM, acquired in 2020 and published in 2022, with heights in metres NAVD88. The aerial is from 2019; these are different historical acquisitions, not one current survey. Local zero for this design exercise is defined at UTM zone 16N easting 306545.847 m, northing 4098094.268 m: 0.00 m local = approximately 94.81 m NAVD88 (recorded DEM sample 94.808303833 m).

Approximate DEM samples, all relative to this same local zero: A −0.16 m, B +0.15 m, C +0.37 m, D −0.15 m; nearby city street −0.37 m; railway embankment +4.48 m; riverbank −1.10 m. These are conceptual terrain references from a 1 m raster, not surveyed point levels. The railway sample is ground/embankment, not a railway clearance or public-walk level. Bare-earth DEM does not establish a thin wall's crest. A water-pixel terrain value is not a measured river level and is not supplied as one.

## Client design requirements and assumptions

- Design flood level: **+3.5 m** in the above local datum (arithmetically about 98.31 m NAVD88). This is an author-defined client scenario, not an official flood level, FEMA base flood elevation, historical high-water mark, tide statistic or regulatory requirement.
- Put habitable floor area above that client flood level. Raise the occupied ground floor and retain **4.5 m** clear height beneath it for an open floodable undercroft. Clear height is the physical distance between proposed ground and the underside of the raised floor; it is not an absolute elevation. Label both the datum-based floor/flood elevations and this clear dimension in the key section.
- Flood protection governs if it conflicts with public access. Work within the marked extent and preserve the barrier and railway. The accessible landward walk/entrance connection is designed without assuming permission to cut through those features.
- Total gross floor area is **6,800 m²**, capable of phased delivery. Combine community reading, a stepped reading hall and evening public life.

No tide regime is asserted for this inland river site. No current legal approval, flood certification, ownership or construction readiness is implied by this design brief.

No commercial NAIP Plus imagery is used.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
---

This schedule records the elements, materials, assemblies and exposure of the selected Direction 02 scheme for RIVER COMMONS, a waterfront public library and summer refuge on a site of approximately 4,563 m² within boundary A–D at Cairo, Illinois, between the city street, the flood barrier, the elevated railway and the Ohio River. The selected scheme comprises two pavilions flanking a 25 m open water court on the street-to-river axis. The water court is a paved public platform at +4.80 m on exposed concrete columns over a floodable undercroft at ±0.000. Glazed links connect the pavilions at +4.80 m and +9.30 m, and the roof level is +13.80 m. The vertical reference is local ±0.000. The enclosed gross floor area is 6,800 m², with 3,400 m² gross and 2,800 m² net per occupied floor. The occupied levels are +4.80 m and +9.30 m. The roof is +13.80 m. The open floodable undercroft is at ±0.000 with 4.5 m clear overhead headroom. The client project flood scenario is +3.5 m. The ground undercroft is outside the enclosed gross floor area total. The waterfront route has a clear width of 4 m. Public vertical circulation comprises one passenger lift and two stairs connecting the ground level and both occupied floors. The material palette is cast-in-place concrete, cross-laminated timber, glulam and aluminum.

This schedule is the reference followed by the enlarged sections, the shading details and the project presentation. It establishes the material and exposure requirements for the selected scheme and is read with the room records, operations, materials and printed identity records of the coordinated architectural submission. It does not describe drawing images; it records the elements, materials, assemblies and exposure in written form.

The building geometry is organized so that the enclosed occupied floors sit above the floodable undercroft. The ground level is an open undercroft at ±0.000 and is not part of the enclosed gross floor area. The occupied floors are at +4.80 m and +9.30 m, each with 3,400 m² gross and 2,800 m² net. The roof is at +13.80 m. The water court platform at +4.80 m forms a paved public platform over exposed concrete columns. The two pavilions flank the water court, and glazed links bridge the court at both occupied levels. The materials in this schedule are limited to cast-in-place concrete, cross-laminated timber, glulam and aluminum. The exposure requirements in this schedule are taken from the client-facts record and are not substituted with alternative materials.

The schedule applies to ground supports, circulation cores, beams, floor decks, window frames, glazing, external shading, the water court platform and the exposed undercroft soffit. It also describes how the floodable undercroft at ±0.000 relates to the client project flood scenario of +3.5 m. The schedule is written in the third person and uses metric units throughout. Where room names are used, they correspond to the room records, including R01 Cooling Commons, R05 Public Support and R06 Reading Room. Where levels are used, they correspond to the notation ±0.000, +4.80 m, +9.30 m and +13.80 m. The purpose of this document is to give a single coordinated written account of the elements, materials, assemblies and exposure for the selected Direction 02 scheme before the enlarged sections, shading details and project presentation are read.

2. GROUND SUPPORTS AND CIRCULATION CORES
---

The ground supports and circulation cores are cast-in-place concrete with an exposed concrete finish. A regular column grid carries the occupied floors. The columns stand in the floodable undercroft at ±0.000, where the clear overhead headroom is 4.5 m. The grid supports the water court platform at +4.80 m, the occupied level at +4.80 m, and the occupied level at +9.30 m. The columns are arranged to suit the two pavilions and the water court, with the open water court spanning 25 m on the street-to-river axis. The cast-in-place concrete columns are exposed concrete. They remain visible in the undercroft and are not concealed by applied finishes in the floodable zone.

The vertical circulation cores are cast-in-place concrete and are exposed concrete. The cores contain the public vertical circulation, comprising one passenger lift and two stairs connecting the ground level and both occupied floors. The cores extend from the ground level at ±0.000 to the occupied levels at +4.80 m and +9.30 m. The cores are part of the structural system that carries the occupied floor decks and stabilizes the pavilions. The exposed concrete finish applies to the core walls and to the visible concrete surfaces within the public route.

The low concrete service block on the east side of the water court platform is cast-in-place concrete with an exposed concrete finish. It holds R05 Public Support, including toilets, drinking-water point, cleaner's room and storage. The service block is coordinated with the single passenger lift and the two stairs. It remains low at the water court platform and does not rise above the occupied building envelope except as required for the public support function. The service block is part of the cast-in-place concrete family of elements, and its visible surfaces are exposed concrete.

The columns and cores are designed for the open undercroft condition. The undercroft at ±0.000 is floodable, and the cast-in-place concrete elements below the client project flood scenario of +3.5 m are fully exposed to the flood condition. The exposed concrete finish is therefore appropriate to the floodable undercroft. The columns and cores do not rely on cross-laminated timber, glulam or aluminum for their primary structural or exposure performance. The cross-laminated timber floors and the glulam beams sit above the columns and cores at the occupied levels. The aluminum window frames and external shading are located above the floodable undercroft and are not part of the ground support system.

The regular column grid is carried through the occupied floors to support the cross-laminated timber decks and the glulam beams. The cast-in-place concrete columns and cores are coordinated with the beams and decks so that the clear heights recorded for the rooms are maintained. The Cooling Commons, the Reading Room and the other occupied rooms have a clear height of 3.6 m as recorded in the room records. The exposed concrete columns and cores contribute to the visible interior character where they occur in the public spaces, including the water court platform and the undercroft. The cast-in-place concrete service block at R05 Public Support is accessed from the public support route and remains separate from the service route used for delivery and staff access.

3. BEAMS
---

The beams are glulam and are exposed. Glulam beams span each occupied floor. The beams carry the cross-laminated timber decks above and are coordinated with the regular cast-in-place concrete column grid. The glulam beams are left exposed in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room. In those rooms, the beams form part of the visible interior together with the cast-in-place concrete supports and the cross-laminated timber soffit. The exposed glulam is not concealed by suspended ceilings in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room. Elsewhere, the glulam beams support the floor structure and may be concealed by floor finishes, services or ceiling zones as required.

The glulam beams occur at the occupied levels at +4.80 m and +9.30 m. They span between cast-in-place concrete columns and cores. The beams are sized and spaced to suit the cross-laminated timber deck and the clear heights of 3.6 m in the room records. The glulam beams are part of the floor assembly that comprises glulam beams, cross-laminated timber deck and floor finish above. In the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room, the glulam beams remain exposed below the cross-laminated timber deck, so the timber soffit remains visible between the beams.

The glulam beams are above the client project flood scenario of +3.5 m. They are at the occupied floors and are not located in the floodable undercroft. The exposed glulam beams in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room are therefore kept above the flood level by the occupied floor elevations. The glulam is left exposed, with no applied finish described in this schedule beyond the exposed glulam condition. The exposed glulam is coordinated with the visible cross-laminated timber soffit and the cast-in-place concrete supports to form the concrete, glulam and cross-laminated timber interior of the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room.

The glulam beams are not substituted with another material. They remain glulam in the assemblies described in this schedule. The beams are coordinated with the external shading where the shading is mounted to the cross-laminated timber floor edges. The glulam beams support the cross-laminated timber deck and provide the structural depth required for the occupied floors. The beams are visible between the cross-laminated timber soffits in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room. The exposed glulam condition applies to the beams in those two rooms and to any other glulam beam that remains visible in the occupied spaces. The glulam beams are part of the load-bearing floor structure and are separate from the aluminum window frames and external shading.

The floor finish above the cross-laminated timber deck is continuous except where openings, stairs and the single passenger lift occur.

The visible cross-laminated timber soffit is not covered in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room. Elsewhere, the underside of the cross-laminated timber deck may be concealed by ceiling or service zones, but the assembly remains glulam beams, cross-laminated timber deck and floor finish above.

The cross-laminated timber deck is part of the occupied floor structure that provides 3,400 m² gross and 2,800 m² net per occupied floor. The floor finish above the cross-laminated timber deck is the upper layer of the assembly. The glulam beams are below the cross-laminated timber deck. The visible timber soffit between the beams in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room is the exposed underside of the cross-laminated timber deck. 8. DURABILITY, FLOOD AND EXPOSURE
---

The floodable open undercroft is at ±0.000. The client project flood scenario is +3.5 m. The cast-in-place concrete columns, circulation cores, water court service block, water court platform structure and exposed undercroft soffit sit at or below the flood level and are therefore fully exposed and floodable. These cast-in-place concrete elements have an exposed concrete finish and are designed to be wet and drained as part of the open undercroft condition. The water court platform is at +4.80 m and therefore sits above the +3.5 m flood scenario, while its supporting columns and the undercroft below remain floodable. The riverbank sampled level is −1.10 m and the railway embankment sampled level is +4.48 m; these levels place the undercroft below the +3.5 m flood scenario and the occupied floors above it.

The occupied floor decks are cross-laminated timber and are at +4.80 m and +9.30 m, above the +3.5 m flood scenario. The glulam beams are at the occupied floors and are exposed in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room; they are kept above the flood level by the occupied floor elevations. The cross-laminated timber floors and the exposed glulam beams are therefore not in the floodable undercroft. The visible timber soffits in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room are protected while remaining visible because they are located above the +3.5 m flood scenario, are part of the occupied floor assembly, and are not enclosed by ceiling finishes in those rooms. The cross-laminated timber soffit remains visible between the glulam beams. The floor finish above the cross-laminated timber deck protects the upper face of the deck, while the visible soffit remains exposed between the beams.

The aluminum window frames and the 2 m aluminum shading fins or canopies are external elements. The aluminum window frames face south, west and the river, and the aluminum shading is fixed outside the south- and west-facing occupied-room glazing with a 2 m projection. Both are exposed to weather and receive finishes selected to match the architectural direction. The aluminum elements are above the flood level at the occupied floors and do not sit in the floodable undercroft. The cast-in-place concrete undercroft elements are the only materials in this schedule that are fully exposed and floodable at ±0.000 against the +3.5 m flood scenario. The water court platform at +4.80 m, the cross-laminated timber floor decks at +4.80 m and +9.30 m, the exposed glulam beams, the aluminum window frames and the aluminum shading are above the flood level and are not floodable.

The exposed concrete undercroft soffit remains visible and floodable in the open undercroft. The cast-in-place concrete columns and cores are exposed to the flood condition and are drained by the open water court platform and undercroft arrangement. The cross-laminated timber and glulam elements are kept above the flood level by the occupied floor elevations and are not exposed to the flood condition. The visible cross-laminated timber soffit between the glulam beams in the Cooling Commons and the Reading Room is protected by its elevation above +3.5 m and by the floor assembly, while it remains visible in those two rooms. The aluminum window frames and the 2 m aluminum shading fins or canopies are external and exposed to weather on the south and west, with selected finishes matching the architectural direction. The aluminum elements are not in the floodable undercroft.

## 8. Design Notes

The north-half workshop strategy places the repair workshop in Z4 so that sewing and pressing are located in the north half of the shop, y = 5.000-10.000 m. S1 and S2 are the two existing off-white sewing machines on timber-topped steel tables, each table 1200 x 600 x 750 mm, with one maker per station and the pedal below. P1 is the existing padded pressing table on steel legs, 1200 x 600 x 900 mm, shared by the two makers. The lightweight workshop divider with an upper glazed portion separates the workshop while keeping the repair process visible. Both sewing-table working surfaces are visible from the customer side of H1 through the upper glazed portion of the workshop divider. The two suspended 25 mm wool-felt acoustic panels AC-01 above S1 and S2 are part of the workshop fit-out. This arrangement keeps the workshop in the north half while allowing customers at the handover counter to see the sewing activity.

The handover sequence at H1 is controlled from the staff side to the west. H1 is the handover counter, fixed within x = 7.400-8.000 m and y = 1.800-3.600 m, 1800 x 600 x 900 mm, top z = 0.900 m. It serves repair intake and collection, and H1 is the collection point in Z1. In the daily state, one customer collects at H1 with one sales assistant present. In the Saturday state, one customer hands over a repair, one customer collects, and one sales assistant is present. The sales assistant stands on the staff side to the west. The printed shop name SECOND SEAM is above entrance D1 and on the handover counter front, so the counter reads as the point of exchange between customer and staff.

The separation of the three garment stores is explicit in the lettering and the capacity schedule. For sale is held on R1-R4 in Z2, with four rails each 1200 x 500 x 1600 mm and each holding 12 garments, giving 48 garments. Awaiting repair is held on AR1 in Z5, with 12 individually identified garment positions at 200 mm centres over 2400 mm, giving 12 garments. Ready to collect is held on RC1 in Z5, with 8 individually identified garment positions at 200 mm centres over 1600 mm, giving 8 garments. The total is 48 + 12 + 8 = 68 garments. Z5 is staff only and provides separate holding for awaiting-repair and completed garments, so the three stores remain distinct in both location and capacity.

The fitting room serves both the sale route and the repair customer. F1 is in Z3, with a clear internal floor of 2000 x 2200 mm and one customer, and it contains a 1500 mm turning circle inside. Z2 includes access to the fitting room, so a customer browsing the sale rail can move to F1 from the sale and browsing zone. The repair customer also passes through the controlled sequence at Z1 for handover and collection, and the same fitting provision is available when that customer moves into the sale and browsing area. In the Saturday state, the one customer approaching the fitting room in Z2 is the same customer then in Z3 for fitting. In this way F1 serves the sale route and the repair customer without merging the three garment stores or the workshop.2f:T5de4,# SECOND SEAM — Material and Lighting Schedule

## 8. Maintenance and Specification Notes

The retained FL-01 existing terrazzo floor is to be kept in a honed matte condition and must remain unpolished. Cleaning and maintenance shall not introduce sealing polishes or any treatment that changes the honed matte appearance. The floor is retained and cleaned, not replaced. During the fit-out, the floor shall be protected from construction traffic, spills and abrasion. Any making good to the floor shall match the surrounding honed matte terrazzo and shall not create a gloss, sheen or sealed patch. The contractor shall ensure that adjacent new joinery, including WD-01 counter facing and storage-unit shelving, is installed without damaging the FL-01 floor and that floor junctions are left clean and made good.

The reclaimed oak WD-01 is to be maintained with a clear, non-yellowing matte varnish. The reclaimed character of the oak is to be preserved, and the finish shall remain clear and matte. Where maintenance requires re-oiling or re-varnishing, the materials used shall be compatible with the reclaimed oak and with the requirement for a clear, non-yellowing matte varnish. The handover counter facing, fitting-room enclosure trim and storage-unit shelving shall be inspected at handover and maintained so that the reclaimed surface remains visible and the matte varnish does not yellow or become glossy. Local repairs to WD-01 shall blend with the surrounding reclaimed oak and shall not introduce a different finish code or sheen.

The PT-01 limewash in colour #D8CCBA is a breathable mineral finish. It is applied to all opaque wall surfaces, including the retained perimeter walls above the skirting and the opaque lower portion of the lightweight workshop divider. Touch-up work shall use the exact colour reference #D8CCBA and shall be carried out so that no visible patch is created. The breathable mineral character of the finish shall be maintained. The contractor shall protect adjacent retained elements and shall not apply PT-01 to glazed portions, including the upper glazed portion of the workshop divider. Where making good is required at retained perimeter walls above the skirting, the repair shall match the PT-01 limewash in #D8CCBA and shall not alter the breathable mineral finish.

The AC-01 wool felt panels are 25 mm thick and are suspended above the two sewing tables S1 and S2.
