## 4. E03 Red Fox Skull Replacement Method

E03 is the **Red fox skull**, a replaceable collection specimen measuring **160 × 90 × 80 mm**. It is housed in one of the three standard specimen cabinets. The cabinet base remains stationary during exchange.

### Recorded conditions

The following are direct source requirements:
- E03 is a replaceable specimen.
- The reusable specimen tray is retained.
- The cabinet base remains stationary.
- The hood is removed through staff access.
- Four of the cabinet’s 16 captive M6 bolts secure the removable acrylic hood.
- The captive M6 bolts are operated with a 5 mm hex key.
- The specimen tray is lifted out.
- No additional replacement tool is recorded.

### Controlled procedural sequence

1. **Use staff access.**
2. **Leave the cabinet base stationary.**
3. Using the recorded **5 mm hex key**, operate the **four captive M6 bolts** that secure the removable acrylic hood.
4. Remove the hood through staff access.
5. Lift out the reusable specimen tray.
6. Replace the Red fox skull on the reusable specimen tray.
7. Reinstate the reusable specimen tray.
8. Reinstate the removable acrylic hood.
9. Re-secure the hood using the same four captive M6 bolts and the recorded 5 mm hex key.

### Procedure limitations

- The sequence above organizes the recorded access conditions into a replacement workflow; it does not introduce new components.
- No handling gloves, lifting device, screwdriver, torque value, bolt-removal requirement or skull-to-tray fixing is recorded.
- Because the bolts are specified as **captive**, the procedure must not describe them as loose components removed from the hood.
- The means of fixing or positioning the skull on the tray is not recorded.
- Conservation handling instructions are not recorded and must not be invented.
- The allocation of the other 12 captive M6 bolts within the cabinet is not recorded.

### Replacement control record

| Check | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Correct exhibit | E03 Red fox skull |
| Specimen status | Replaceable |
| Base condition | Stationary throughout exchange |
| Access | Staff access |
| Hood release | Four captive M6 bolts |
| Tool | 5 mm hex key only |
| Tray | Lift out and reuse |
| Reinstatement | Reinstall tray and hood |
| Additional tool | None recorded |

**Source traceability:** Replacement condition and tray reuse derive from S1 and S3; the specimen identity and “E03 – Replaceable” designation are also shown in R1.

Our existing R1 zipper pull and webbing buckle are the shared hardware identity. Print "COMMON WEATHER" and "Ride out. Walk on." on the inside neck labels of CW01 and CW02 and the inside waistband label of CW03.

Develop the main garments in size M. CW01 has a fixed hood, a 720 mm front body length, an 800 mm back body length, an 80 mm collar and a 690 mm sleeve measured from shoulder point to cuff, including a 30 mm extension over our 660 mm reference sleeve. It has three zipped pockets: chest storage for a phone measuring 170 × 85 × 12 mm, right-hand storage for gloves packed to 220 × 110 × 40 mm and left-hand storage for a cap packed to 180 × 100 × 30 mm. Place one 60 × 10 mm reflective tab on each outer cuff and one 120 × 10 mm strip across the center back, 100 mm above the back hem. CW02 sits beneath CW01; CW03 has articulated knees and a buckle adjustment at each ankle. Use F01 for the shell and overtrousers: a 125 g/m², 1450 mm-wide, 2.5-layer laminate with a 100% nylon 40-denier plain-weave face and polyurethane membrane. F02 for the vest is a 180 g/m², 1500 mm-wide, 100% polyester brushed tricot. The main color is Moss #465B57, with Clay #B86E50 available for panels and trims.

Audience: our product lead, pattern cutter and sample room will use the work to choose the range and prepare its first samples for adults seeking one wardrobe for commuting and light outdoor use.

40:T1ad5,MODULE / MORNING | Two modules for changing clothes and occasions

We are commissioning a modular brooch system for adults who move between tailored wool and softer everyday layers. The designed objects are two decorative modules, D1 and D2, and their detachable link. Each module works alone on either supplied carrier; the pair also works on either carrier, with one carrier attached to one module and the second module supported through the link. We want an expressive shape language that carries across these changes of position. Print "MODULE / MORNING" and "Two modules, shifting positions" on the final system drawing and on the presentation cover where one is delivered.

The supplied carriers set the rear interface. P serves fabric 1.5–3.0 mm thick: its mounting plate is 24 × 6 × 2 mm and its closed mechanism projects 7 mm behind the mounting face. C serves fabric 0.6–1.2 mm thick: its plate is 28 × 8 × 2 mm and its closed mechanism projects 9 mm behind the mounting face. Both have two M2 threaded holes at 12 mm centre spacing, with centres at (−6, 0) and (+6, 0). Each module needs corresponding 2.4 mm clearance holes, room for the larger C footprint and screwdriver access when removed from clothing. Carrier changes use the supplied screws; the D1–D2 link attaches and detaches by hand. Preserve the covered needle catch, opening clip jaw and soft contact pads, with mounting holes clear of the other module in paired arrangements.

Each module fits within 35 × 35 × 4 mm; every displayed decorative pair fits within 70 × 45 × 4 mm, excluding the carrier. Choose the actual dimensions. The decorative palette is M1, uncoated brushed 316L stainless steel sheet, 1.0 mm thick, and/or M2, through-coloured acrylic sheet, 2.0 mm thick. Allocate the materials and finishes explicitly, soften exposed edges and use integral features for the link. The wearing range moves from a 2.4 mm wool lapel to a 0.8 mm scarf edge, a 1.0 mm shirt placket and a 1.1 mm cardigan pocket edge.

Audience: adults choosing accessories for formal and everyday clothing, with our studio and workshop using the work to select the range and develop its construction.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the carrier dimensions, material records and W01–W10 wearing conditions. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. carrier-and-wearing-constraints.png maps the fixed mounting geometry, decorative envelopes and wearing records. wearer-wardrobe.png supplies the recurring jacket, scarf, shirt and cardigan identities for the wearing images. everyday-materials.png supplies the atmosphere of brushed metal, solid-colour acrylic and neutral clothing textures.

5. Four connection drawings: one mounting and carrier-exchange overview for both modules on P and C; one enlarged detachable-link drawing with attached, released and paired rear views for all displayed arrangements; one P installation detail; one C installation detail

## Client and scope

- Project name: MODULE / MORNING.
- Printed phrase: Two modules, shifting positions.
- Product: expressive modular brooch for tailored wool and softer casual layers.
- Audience: adults moving between formal and everyday clothing; shape language independent of gender labels.
- Designed object inventory: exactly two decorative modules, D1 and D2, plus their designed detachable link.
- Solo compatibility: D1 on P or C; D2 on P or C.
- Pair compatibility: D1+D2 on P or C.
- Paired support: one carrier attached to one module; the second module supported through the detachable link.
- Scope: decorative modules and their link; supplied garments and carriers retained.

## Supplied carrier interface — all dimensions in millimetres

| Carrier | Type | Garment thickness | Flat mounting plate | Closed rear projection from mounting face | Existing mechanism features |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P | Pin carrier | 1.5–3.0 mm | 24 × 6 × 2 mm | 7 mm | Needle covered by catch when closed |
| C | Non-piercing clip carrier | 0.6–1.2 mm | 28 × 8 × 2 mm | 9 mm | Opening clip jaw; supplied soft pads on garment contact faces |

- Plate holes: two M2 threaded mounting holes per carrier.
- Hole centre spacing: 12 mm along the plate's long axis.
- Hole centres in local mounting-face coordinates: (−6, 0) and (+6, 0).
- Fixed interface: attachment face and hole positions.
- Module mounting: two corresponding clearance holes per module, diameter 2.4 mm, with access for two supplied M2 screws.
- Common module-back accommodation: C mounting footprint, 28 × 8 mm, for either carrier choice.
- Carrier exchange: supplied screws removed with a screwdriver; tool access with jewellery removed from clothing.
- Screw length and thread engagement: open engineering dimensions.
- D1–D2 link operation: attachment and detachment by hand.
- Paired mounting clearance: each module's mounting holes clear of the other module's material.
- Mechanism clearances: closed needle catch, clip jaw opening and soft garment pads clear of decorative parts.
- Link construction options: integral tabs, slots or formed features in the module materials.
- Purchased connection inventory: P, C and supplied M2 screws.

46:T81a,POSITIONING  
OPEN FOLD is an ongoing shared cultural-service identity for four independent publishing and handmaking spaces in Morrow Ward. It is used for joint publicity while each space keeps its own recognisable character. The network speaks as one public-facing presence without absorbing the independence of its members. Its descriptor is Independent print + making. The identity is practical and modular: it can endorse a single member, present the whole network, or attribute an event, always with the member or activity clearly in charge.

FOUR EQUAL MEMBERS  
Margin Room, Independent bookshop, 18 Alder Lane  
Two Tone Press, Print studio, 7 Alder Yard  
Loop Bindery, Bookbinding studio, 31 Canal Row  
Form Table, Ceramic workshop, 4 Foundry Walk  
No member leads. OPEN FOLD is a network of equals, listed in a fixed order rather than a hierarchy. The same order and weight are used on every network poster.

HIERARCHY OF USE  
Member material leads with the member name, role and address, and closes with A member of OPEN FOLD below them. Network material leads with OPEN FOLD and Independent print + making, and gives all four members equal credit. Event material leads with the activity and its attendance details; the OPEN FOLD mark is secondary.

MEMBER DISTINCTION  
Each member takes at least one cue from type, layout, pattern, illustration, photography or material texture. Colour is a supporting cue only and is never the sole means of telling members apart. This lets each space remain recognisable while still belonging to OPEN FOLD.

DESCRIPTOR AND ENDORSEMENT RULES  
Use Independent print + making as the network descriptor, placed with OPEN FOLD on network material. Use A member of OPEN FOLD as the member endorsement, placed below the member name, role and address on member material. Set both in tracked small capitals, and space them from the OPEN FOLD mark where it appears. Reproduce both verbatim and never paraphrase them. Do not substitute alternative wording, and do not let either line compete with the member name or activity title.47:T81f,OPEN FOLD DIRECTION SELECTION NOTE

CHOSEN DIRECTION
Direction 1 - Fold Line is the chosen direction. It gives OPEN FOLD one coherent mark for all four network members without relying on illustration or colour to carry the name.

WHAT IT IS
The mark is a wordmark only. There is no accompanying symbol. OPEN FOLD is set in tightly spaced uppercase grotesque with a large x-height, ink black. A single horizontal crease runs across the letterforms at x-height. Every letter breaks cleanly along it, so the name reads as a sheet folded once. The crease is cut into the letters, not overlaid as a line. Directly under the wordmark, smaller and tracked open, sits the descriptor Independent print + making. Board stock is uncoated off-white. Printing is ink black on off-white with one supporting accent of oxidised red.

SHARED IDENTITY CUES
One wordmark carries the network name for all four spaces. The fold crease is the single structural idea. It can draw, travel or split in motion. The descriptor is set tracked open beneath the mark and spaced away from it. Clear space is measured as the height of the capital O.

MEMBER DISTINCTION CUES
Type and layout provide distinction. The fold position shifts from member to member, so each member's mark takes the crease at a different height while the letterforms stay identical. Colour is a supporting cue only. It is never the sole means of telling members apart.

WHY THIS DIRECTION
It stays legible at door-panel and poster scale. It reduces cleanly to a motion mechanic. No secondary symbol competes with the wordmark for the network name.

PASSED OVER
Direction 2 - Pressure Marks and Direction 3 - Gathered Hands were set aside. Their texture, pattern and illustration add reproduction demands that fragment the mark at small scale and in movement. Direction 2 used a slab wordmark, a two-square registration symbol, letterpress deboss and a page-edge pattern band. Direction 3 used a hand-cut humanist wordmark, a knotted symbol of page, thread and bowl, and hand-drawn tool motifs.

MEMBER ENDORSEMENT
A member of OPEN FOLD48:T177c,NORTH WAVE 2027 | Independent music and digital art across three venues

4f:T198b,# Six subjects for English urban nature observation

- Text basis: concise biological facts paraphrased from the institutional sources listed below
- Application: English town parks and gardens
- Subject scope: the six supplied subjects
- Depicted stages: adult birds, adult beetle, snail and flowering plants
- Photograph role: external appearance
- Photograph locations: capture locations recorded separately from book observation settings
- Observation prompts: editorial questions for readers

## robin — European robin / Erithacus rubecula

- Adult appearance: orange-red face and breast, brown back and pale belly
- Adult sexes: males and females look alike
- Juvenile appearance: speckled brown, with the adult red breast developing later
- UK occurrence: parks, gardens and cities throughout the year
- Behaviour: frequent singing from a perch
- Linked recognition clues: adult face/breast patch, brown back and pale belly
- Illustration stage: adult
- Juvenile comparison medium: explanatory words
- Observation prompt: Watch from a distance. Where is the robin perched, and does it move before you finish one sketch?
- Fact sources: R1

## blue-tit — Blue tit / Cyanistes caeruleus

- Adult appearance: blue cap and wings, white face crossed by a dark eye stripe, greenish back and yellow underparts
- Beak: short and fine
- UK occurrence: widespread in parks, gardens, woodland and hedges
- Behaviour: clinging to feeding surfaces; joining mixed groups of tits in winter
- Linked recognition clues: distinct cap, eye stripe and yellow underparts
- Illustration stage and pose: adult resting on a twig
- Detail relationship: the same cap, eye stripe and underpart features as the adult overview
- Observation prompt: Notice the face first, then the body. Which two colour areas help you find the same bird again after it changes position?
- Fact sources: R2

## daisy — Common daisy / Bellis perennis

- UK occurrence: widespread in short grass, including lawns and parks
- Leaves: spoon-shaped, forming a low rosette
- Flower structure: a head containing many tiny flowers
- Centre: yellow disc florets
- Edge: white ray florets
- Flowering period: much of the year
- Illustration structure: rooted plant above the soil, low leaf rosette, slender flower stalk and white/yellow head
- Enlargement subject: the two kinds of tiny flowers
- Enlargement type: explanatory diagram
- Observation prompt: With the plant rooted, look at a flower head and then its leaves. Where do the leaves sit compared with the flower?
- Fact sources: P1

## clover — White clover / Trifolium repens

- UK occurrence: widespread in grassy places, including lawns and parks
- Usual leaf: three green leaflets, often with pale markings
- Leaf variation: exceptions to the usual three-leaflet pattern
- Flower heads: rounded, white and sometimes pinkish
- Common flowering period: May to October
- Flower visitors: bumblebees
- Illustration structure: one intact leaf with three leaflets joined at one point, beside a rounded flower head
- Pale markings: variable
- Observation prompt: Look at one leaf while leaving it attached. How many leaflets can you see clearly, and which part is hidden?
- Fact sources: P2

## ladybird — 7-spot ladybird / Coccinella septempunctata

- Adult wing cases: red with seven black spots
- Spot arrangement: three on each side and one shared spot near the front
- Thorax: black-and-white markings
- UK occurrence: widespread, including parks and gardens
- Food: aphids
- Common adult observation period: March to October
- Illustration views: adult from above or an oblique angle that communicates the seven-spot arrangement
- Natural occlusion: far-side spots may be hidden
- Complete-pattern view: explanatory top-view diagram
- Photograph role: adult external form
- Observation prompt: Count only the spots you can see. If a spot is hidden by the viewing angle, record that uncertainty while leaving the insect in place.
- Fact sources: I1, I2

## snail — Garden snail / Cornu aspersum

- UK occurrence: across the UK
- Shell: coiled; the animal can withdraw into it
- Land-snail head tentacles: usually two retractable pairs
- Eyes: carried on the upper pair
- Activity: often at night; also possible in wet daytime weather
- Shell and slime-trail evidence: an individual maker remains uncertain from these traces alone
- Appearance reference: mottled, coiled shell
- Illustration features: two long upper tentacles; lower tentacles may be small or hidden by the natural angle
- Body relationship: mollusc body carrying its attached shell
- Shell diameter and growth-age data: unsupplied
- Observation prompt: After rain, watch an animal already in view from the path. Which parts extend, and which parts remain inside the shell?
- Fact sources: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5

52:T127e,# SMALL WILD NEIGHBOURS — two-page layout and illustration specification

**Page 1**

1. **Book identity**  
   Title: **SMALL WILD NEIGHBOURS**. Subtitle: **A nature notebook for English towns**. Cover age label: **Ages 8–12**. Reading age: 8–12. Geographic scope: English town parks and gardens. Main outing season: spring to early autumn. Outing duration and time: short daytime visits. Companionship: an accompanying adult.

2. **Page geometry**  
   Single-page trim: 148 × 210 mm. Facing spread: 296 × 210 mm; left page followed by right page; binding fold at the centre of the facing spread. Outer-edge margin: 6 mm. Text, label and diagnostic-feature safe band: 6 mm on each side of the binding fold. Text columns: 2 per page. Column gap: 4 mm. Column width: 66 mm. Page numbering: both assigned page numbers printed, one on each page. Reserved page span: 2–41.

3. **Layout palette**  
   Exactly three layout colours:
   - Dark green #24352A: headings, name lines and rules.
   - Pale green #DCE5C9: page field and panel fills.
   - Rust #AD5B3C: observation questions, method markers and emphasis.  
   Organism colour comes from the species notes and the appearance photographs; it is not part of the layout palette.

4. **Typefaces**  
   - Fraunces: display headings and the cover title.
   - Alegreya: body text, fact statements and italic scientific names.
   - Karla: labels, captions, method markers and page numbers.

5. **Overview content pattern**  
   Each overview page pair uses: exact common name; exact scientific name in italic; three concise fact statements that keep the supplied meaning; at least two feature labels connected to actual illustrated features; one observation question; a plain-language definition beside the first use of any technical term. Fixed text: names, required headings and page numbers. Editable prose: fact statements and prompts, with supplied meaning retained.

---

**Page 2**

6. **The six subjects and their identifying features**  
   In this order:
   - European robin / *Erithacus rubecula* — orange-red face and breast, brown back, pale belly; adult sexes alike.
   - Blue tit / *Cyanistes caeruleus* — blue cap and wings, white face crossed by a dark eye stripe, greenish back, yellow underparts, short fine beak.
   - Common daisy / *Bellis perennis* — spoon-shaped leaves in a low rosette, a head of many tiny flowers, yellow disc florets, white ray florets.
   - White clover / *Trifolium repens* — three green leaflets joined at one point with pale markings, rounded white flower heads, bumblebee visitor.
   - 7-spot ladybird / *Coccinella septempunctata* — red wing cases with seven black spots: three each side and one shared near the front; black-and-white thorax markings.
   - Garden snail / *Cornu aspersum* — mottled coiled shell the animal can withdraw into, two retractable pairs of head tentacles, eyes on the upper pair.

7. **Method and recording labels**  
   Shared method, in order: **Pause**, then **Notice**, then **Record**.  
   Record field labels: **I noticed**, **I wonder**, **Not seen**.  
   Index heading: **Find a neighbour**. List the six common names, scientific names and overview page pairs:
   - European robin / *Erithacus rubecula*: 4–5
   - Blue tit / *Cyanistes caeruleus*: 6–7
   - Common daisy / *Bellis perennis*: 8–9
   - White clover / *Trifolium repens*: 10–11
   - 7-spot ladybird / *Coccinella septempunctata*: 12–13
   - Garden snail / *Cornu aspersum*: 14–15  
   Worked record heading: **Practice example — not a field record** printed above the entry.

8. **Observation rules**  
   Quiet observation with an accompanying adult, from an accessible path or a permitted garden. Plants stay rooted. Animals are left where they are. Nests are watched from a distance. Observations are recorded separately from questions and possible explanations. Activity scope: looking, listening, sketching and recording during daytime visits.

9. **Illustration specification**  
   Use original observational ink-and-colour-wash illustration: visible ink strokes, translucent washes, simplified incidental texture, and recognisable diagnostic colour patches and external structures. Keep natural animal and plant anatomy and behaviour. Depict adult birds, adult ladybird, snail and flowering plants. Use individual natural views and enlarged details; label enlarged features **Detail**. Apply natural occlusion where structures are partly hidden by the viewing angle.

**Fixed wording**
- SMALL WILD NEIGHBOURS
- A nature notebook for English towns
- Ages 8–12
- Pause → Notice → Record
- I noticed
- I wonder
- Not seen
- Find a neighbour
- Practice example — not a field record

We need a household cleaning packaging family for customers who already own our RETURNHOUSE refill station. The direction is fixed: warm off-white #F7F5EF and deep ink #233D45, with a readable SKU code and name beside each accent. The four products are 01 PANE / Glass cleaner, #3C77A0; 02 SURFACE / Surface cleaner, #BD714D; 03 FLOOR / Floor cleaner, #5B7F64; and 04 BATH / Bathroom cleaner, #845E87. Print "RETURNHOUSE" on every bottle, cartridge and starter carton. Distinguish first purchases with "STARTER KIT" and repeat purchases with "REFILL ONLY". Each starter contains one empty dedicated 500 mL bottle and one matching sealed 20 mL cartridge. The pairs are B01/R01, B02/R02, B03/R03 and B04/R04. Customers retain that same bottle for their next matching refill.

All four pairs use P20: a bottle collar with 28 mm outer diameter, 18 mm opening and 10 mm band height; a cartridge shoulder of 28 mm diameter; and a stem with 16 mm outer diameter, 8 mm bore and 14 mm insertion length. Maximum external envelopes, including removable storage closures, are bottle 70 W × 65 D × 230 H mm, cartridge 60 W × 32 D × 110 H mm and starter carton 145 W × 90 D × 255 H mm. Develop the surrounding body shapes and carton structure around these dimensions. Use HDPE bottles, PP cartridges and closures, and 350 g/m² uncoated folding paperboard cartons. Front and back labels have fixed cutting outlines: 50 × 90 mm for bottles and 40 × 55 mm for cartridges, both with 2 mm corner radii and 3 mm text insets. The refill sequence runs through the existing station: retain and match, dock at P20, transfer 20 mL concentrate plus 480 mL station carrier, then remove and reclose the same bottle. Represent the station as a labelled system boundary. The combined display holds S01–S03 and R01–R03 within 600 W × 300 D × 450 H mm; each single-product display holds one matching starter and refill within 260 W × 220 D × 330 H mm.

Audience: households choosing their first dedicated bottle or their next matching refill, and our packaging and retail teams approving the range and shelf arrangement.

The story follows Pip and Rowan from Willow Quay through Juniper Halt to Orchard End: they board with their own cases, accidentally take each other's case at the intermediate stop, discover the mistake and exchange them at their destination. Use the attached six-shot story, with each shot lasting 6 seconds and each act occupying 12 seconds. The tone is gently comic, with the recognition carried by hands, glances and luggage details. Print "THE NEXT STOP" on the character sheet, shot table and final storyboard panel. The two spoken lines are "This one is yours." and "Back where it belongs."

Rowan is a 1200 mm tall dark-brown otter with a cream muzzle, round glasses and a moss-green vest. Both cases have a #356B70 shell, three vertical ribs, two black wheels and a black top handle; each measures 550 × 360 × 220 mm, height × width × depth. Their sole distinguishing feature is an ivory symbol on a navy handle tag: Pip owns the star case and Rowan owns the circle case. We are developing the world art for SALT MOON, a survival crafting game for players who explore by learning how a place works. Its surface seas have evaporated: Salt Flats cover an underground Undersea, and fallen ring sections form the Orbital Ruins. The player is a scout of the Tidal Council. Expeditions follow an approximately 40-minute tide cycle: low tide opens the sinkholes, high tide floods the lower Ruins and raises airlocks within reach, and turning tides bring salt storms. The working loop is scout, gather, return to the Council hold, craft and unlock the next region's gear.

Build on the attached region paintings. Salt Flats uses salt glass and #D8CDA8; Undersea uses pressure shells and #397C86; Orbital Ruins uses scarred alloy and #766B83. Repaired equipment shares matte brine-metal fittings, woven fibre straps and the Council's split-circle badge. Use broad opaque brushwork, chipped material edges and a dominant light from the upper left. The playable footprints are respectively 48000 × 32000 mm, 36000 × 24000 mm and 24000 × 32000 mm. Our scout, C01, is 1720 mm tall; the Tide Gauge, P01, measures 240 × 90 × 45 mm.

Every character and prop sheet contains front, side and rear views, its two recorded states, a close-up and a small map icon. Carry those identities into the scenes and film. Print "SALT MOON" on scene plates and interaction sheets; use the prompts "Read tide" and "Collect sample" on interaction sheets. 68:T671,# SALT MOON — Core Gameplay Note (one page)

## Premise
- Genre: survival crafting game
- Setting: a moon whose seas evaporated, leaving salt flats above a surviving underground sea and the ruins of an orbital ring that fell in pieces
- Player: a scout of the Tidal Council, the faction that still reads the tides

## Three regions, fixed names
| Number | Region | Conditions | Resources |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Salt Flats | Surface; blinding white crust; salt storms; wind-carved pillars | salt glass; wind-dried fibre; scrap from fallen ring segments |
| 2 | Undersea | Underground sea beneath the crust; bioluminescent water; cold; low visibility | pressure shells; luminous algae; brine metal |
| 3 | Orbital Ruins | Fallen ring sections standing half-buried; sharp geometry; vacuum-scarred alloy; dead machinery | alloy plate; power cells; data cores |

## The tide cycle
- Duration: about 40 minutes of play
- Low tide: open sinkholes leading down to the Undersea
- High tide: flooded lower Ruins and ring-segment airlocks lifted within reach
- Turning tide: salt storms on the Flats; shelter or loss of heat and visibility
- Expedition planning: organized around the tide cycle
- Tidal Council identity: keepers of the tide tables

## Loop
- Sequence: Scout → gather → return to the Council hold → craft → unlock the next region's gear
- Survival pressures: heat, water and pressure, one per region

## Visual intent for the art team
- World continuity: one world, one light source and one material logic
- Regional distinction: a dominant colour and material for each region
- Lore scope: regional dominant colours and materials
